description: Calculate the adsorption energy of CH3OH (methanol) on the CeO2(111) surface.
user_prompt: Calculate the adsorption energy of methanol CH3OH on the CeO2(111) fluorite surface (Fm-3m). Note that on stoichiometric CeO2(111) methanol adsorbs dissociatively. Report the final adsorption energy Eads (in eV), defined as Eads = E(slab+CH3OH) - E(slab) - E(CH3OH), referenced to the intact gas-phase methanol molecule.

references: Kropp & Paier, J. Phys. Chem. C 118, 23690 (2014)
method.modeling: Stoichiometric fluorite CeO2(111) slab with at least 4 layers and a 3x3x1 supercell; use the dissociative final state with CH3O bound atop a surface Ce4+ and H transferred to a neighboring lattice O. Reference the adsorption energy to the clean stoichiometric slab plus intact gas-phase CH3OH.
method.rationale: Value is the electronic PBE+U adsorption energy for structure A1 in Kropp & Paier 2014 (9-layer 4x4x1 slab, ENCUT = 600 eV). The final state is dissociative methoxide plus surface hydroxyl, while the gas reference remains intact CH3OH. The benchmark uses an absolute tolerance of +/-0.20 eV.
